title: Learner 01 | Day 001: Files, folders, and the interpreter
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> ## Question of the Day
> After the example below: When does the function body run? Why does `return` not display the text itself?

## Goal

Show the **project name** on LearnForge’s onboarding screen.

## Learn this first

Open `src/learnforge/experience/onboarding/project_title.py`. It already contains this small function:

```python
def project_title():
    project_name = "Pending"
    return project_name
```

- `def` gives the function a name. Its body waits until the app calls it. `()` means it receives no arguments.
- The four spaces put the next two lines inside the function. `=` connects the variable `project_name` to a value. Quotes mark text.
- `return` gives that value back to the caller. It does not print. The app displays the returned value.

## Your change and method signature

**File:** `src/learnforge/experience/onboarding/project_title.py`  
**Function:** `project_title()` — no arguments; returns text (`str`).

Change only `project_name` from `"Pending"` to **`"LearnForge"`**. Keep the function name and indentation.

## Test inputs and expected results

| Case | Expected result |
|---|---|
| Call `project_title()` after your edit | Returns `"LearnForge"` |
| Run `python run_demo.py onboarding` | Your screen line is `Project: LearnForge` |
| Temporarily use another text value | The returned value and your screen line both change; restore `"LearnForge"` afterward |

## Scope

One function. No arguments, printing inside it, user input, dictionaries, classes or edits to another feature.

## Research hints

1. Search `Python assignment variable string number` in the [Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3.13/tutorial/).
2. Search `Python def indentation return versus print`; read one small example, not the whole manual.
3. Predict the changed-value result, run it, and explain which name/value changed and why the screen changed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The function returns the exact value above and the app displays the expected line.
- [ ] Show the actual command/output for the normal and changed-value runs.



**Review with @YogeshPatil991:** trace each line: purpose → value before → value after (or no change) → why → contribution to the screen.

<details><summary>Small execution picture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Call["App calls the function"] --> Name["Local variable gets a value"]
  Name --> Return["return gives it to the app"]
  Return --> Screen["App displays your line"]
```

This shows call order and values, not physical memory addresses or measured CPU activity.
</details>
architecture_topic: Separate stored instructions from a running process. A stopped process cannot remember yesterday's variables.
placement_reason: A small welcome-screen value producer; the provided runner owns printing.
inline_teaching: The issue contains the complete first-function lesson and execution picture.
